validity.researcher_notes: P2626 is the Trail West/N-MAX project: a proposed ~106-mile, 30-inch interstate gas transmission lateral that would have run from an interconnection with GTN's (Gas Transmission Northwest) system near Madras, Oregon to Northwest Pipeline's (Williams) Grants Pass Lateral near Molalla, Oregon, delivering gas toward the Portland-area market. It was a joint-venture project of Trail West Pipeline, LLC (TWP) / Trail West Holdings (TWH) -- 50% NWN Energy (a NW Natural Holdings subsidiary) and 50% TransCanada American Investments Ltd (a TransCanada/TC Energy subsidiary) -- independently confirmed by two differently-authored, differently-dated sources: Bark, a Mt. Hood-area conservation nonprofit (bark-out.org, page dated 2020-03-10) and Sightline Institute, a Pacific Northwest policy think tank (sightline.org, 2019-06-06 article). Both independently state the same design capacity (500 MMcf/d, doubleable), 30-inch diameter, and 'late 2023' target in-service date, and EIA's Natural Gas Pipeline Projects tracker (28 releases, May 2018 - Aug 2026) independently lists a matching FERC-authority 'Trail West/N-MAX' project (106 miles, $800M, 450 MMcf/d additional capacity, OR-OR, operator of record 'Northwest Pipeline Co'). This is a genuine, distinct sub-project on the Williams Northwest Pipeline system -- NOT a duplicate of any of the other four 'Northwest Gas Pipeline' rows in this batch: P0230 is the aggregate ~3,900-mile NWP system row; P5101 is the Kalama Lateral; P7790 is the Kelso-Beaver Reliability Project; P7812 is the Wild Trail project. No cross_row_leads found this session for those siblings (search-engine access was budget-exhausted and oilandgaswatch.org / S&P Global / Internet Archive were all unreachable this session -- see individual fill notes). Two caveats filed separately below: (1) the sheet's CancelledYear (2023) is not what EIA's release history actually shows -- corrected to 2022 (spec concern); (2) the sheet's Owner (Williams Companies, 100%) is contradicted by both independent sources naming the actual TWP/TWH joint-venture sponsors (attribution concern); (3) EndLocation (Portland) is a market-delivery generalization -- Bark's literal, and the route geojson's, terminus is Molalla, OR (spec concern, corrected in the Location fill directly).

The sheet's CancelledYear (2023) is not supported by any source found, including its own cited ref (the generic eia.gov/naturalgas/data.php#pipelines landing page states no year at all). EIA's dated release history is unambiguous: the project shows status 'Announced' in every release from 2018-05 through 2021-10, then flips to 'Cancelled/On Hold' starting with the 2022-01 release (file EIA-NaturalGasPipelineProjects_Jan2022.xlsx), and its last_updated_date field is frozen at 2022-01-14 in every subsequent release through 2026-08 -- i.e. EIA has recorded no change to this project's status in 4.5+ years. Per this repo's own EIA-source convention ('the first release showing Completed or Cancelled bounds the in-service or cancellation year'), the correct CancelledYear is 2022, not 2023. (gem.wiki's own uncitable page claims a 'July 2023 EIA update' for this project, which appears to be a stale/incorrect paraphrase of the same EIA history -- not independently verified and not usable as a source regardless.) I could not find a second, non-EIA origin (news release, FERC docket withdrawal, or operator statement) confirming the cancellation -- Bark (2020) and Sightline (2019) both predate it, oilandgaswatch.org 404'd, S&P Global 403'd, and Internet Archive/Wayback returned 429s all session (concurrent-session rate limiting) so no capture could be pulled for any of those. Tier stays medium (EIA is one origin) despite high confidence in the correction.

validity.recommendation: Replace Owner1 (Williams Companies, 100%) with the TWP/TWH joint-venture sponsors.
validity.researcher_notes: The sheet records Owner1 = Williams Companies at 100%, with no ref. Two independent sources both explicitly and consistently describe a DIFFERENT ownership structure for this specific sub-project: Trail West Pipeline, LLC (TWP), a wholly-owned subsidiary of Trail West Holdings (TWH), is 50% owned by NWN Energy (a wholly-owned subsidiary of NW Natural Holdings) and 50% owned by TransCanada American Investments Ltd (an indirect wholly-owned subsidiary of TransCanada Corporation, renamed TC Energy in 2019). Neither source mentions Williams/Northwest Pipeline as an owner of this new lateral at all -- NWP is referenced only as the EXISTING system this new pipe would interconnect with (via NWP's Grants Pass Lateral near Molalla), which is a routing/interconnection fact, not an ownership one. This is analogous to the batch's cluster-warning pattern: a whole-system attribute (Williams owns the NWP mainline, P0230) appears to have been copied onto this distinct JV sub-project's row. One tension worth flagging: EIA's own tracker lists the operator of record as 'Northwest Pipeline Co' for this project -- I read this as EIA's administrative/regulatory tracking convention (the project would ultimately be certificated as part of NWP's FERC jurisdiction) rather than a true ownership claim, since it directly conflicts with two independent, specific, differently-dated descriptions of the JV structure and neither Bark nor Sightline is a low-quality source. Tier high: Bark and Sightline are differently authored, differently dated, and agree exactly on the JV structure and percentages.

validity.recommendation: Corroborate or drop the 500 MMcf/d design-capacity figure; current sheet value (450) matches EIA's 'additional capacity' field but not the two secondary sources' stated design capacity.
validity.researcher_notes: Sheet Capacity (450 MMcf/d) matches EIA's 'Additional Capacity' field exactly across all 28 releases. However, both Bark and Sightline independently and identically state the pipeline 'is designed to transport 500 million cubic feet per day with an option to double that amount in the future' -- a real, unresolved numeric conflict, not rounding. Plausible explanation (not confirmed): EIA's project_type for this row is 'Expansion' and its own documentation defines 'Additional Capacity' for an expansion as the INCREMENTAL capacity added to the broader system, not the new pipe's own full nameplate/design rating -- so 450 and 500 may describe different scopes (incremental system capacity vs. the 30-inch pipe's design capacity) rather than one of them being simply wrong. I could not reach a primary FERC docket (no docket number is on file -- EIA's docket_number field reads 'na' for this project in every release) to adjudicate definitively; WebSearch was budget-exhausted and search-engine scraping (DuckDuckGo, Bing) was unproductive this session. Left the sheet's 450 as REVERIFIED (matches EIA) and flag 500 here as the candidate/alternate figure for reviewer judgment, tier high because two independent, differently-authored sources agree exactly on 500.
